node-1.label: Patient had intermittent fevers for one month

node-2.label: Patient is a 19-year-old white female college student with unremarkable medical and dental history and no history of alcohol or illicit drug use

node-3.label: Patient has a one-week history of occipital headache and a one-month history of intermittent right calf pain and generalized malaise

node-4.label: Physical examination reveals temperature of 39°C, a diastolic murmur in the left parasternal area, and a pansystolic murmur at the apex

why.why: Blood culture is positive for gram-positive streptococci, and transesophageal echocardiography shows a 3 cm vegetation on the aortic valve with severe aortic regurgitation and anterior mitral leaflet perforation with moderate regurgitation. These provide direct microbiological and structural evidence for infective endocarditis. The prolonged fever, occipital headache, right calf pain, and cardiac murmurs are consistent with valvular infection and embolic phenomena, and both laboratory and radiology expert analyses confirm the diagnosis. Confidence is raised from 0.8 to 0.95.

Although the patient's age, fever, malaise, calf pain, and regurgitant murmurs initially suggested acute rheumatic fever, the positive blood culture for gram-positive streptococci and the echocardiographic finding of a large aortic valve vegetation with mitral perforation are diagnostic of infective endocarditis. Expert analyses note that acute rheumatic fever lacks supporting evidence, so confidence is reduced from 0.12 to 0.03.

The young female demographic and multi-system presentation initially raised the possibility of autoimmune/rheumatic disease, but the confirmed blood culture and transesophageal echocardiographic findings establish infective endocarditis. Expert analyses find no supporting evidence for autoimmune/rheumatic disease, so confidence is reduced from 0.08 to 0.02.

Expert laboratory and radiology analyses both conclude that these findings are diagnostic, and the clinical features of prolonged fever, headache, calf pain, and cardiac murmurs are consistent.

why.why: Brain MRI revealed a cortical infarct, and vascular imaging showed a right peroneal mycotic aneurysm and brachial artery occlusion, providing direct imaging confirmation of embolic complications from the aortic valve vegetation. The occipital headache and right calf pain are explained by these emboli, and both laboratory and radiology expert analyses confirm this interpretation. Dedicated imaging has now been performed, so confidence is raised from 0.65 to 0.95.
